quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Why should you use both front and rear brakes every time you slow down or stop?

options.text: Using only one brake will cause the brakes to wear unevenly.
It builds good braking habits for emergencies.
Using both brakes is the only way to slow down a motorcycle.
The brakes only work when both are applied.

questions.correctAnswerText: It builds good braking habits for emergencies.
questions.explanation: Using both brakes during normal stops helps you develop a habit of always using both. In emergencies, this habit will help you react correctly when using both brakes may be critical.

questions.question: When should you flash your brake light?

options.text: When you are tired while riding.
When you will slow down where other drivers won't expect it.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you will slow down where other drivers won't expect it.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle brake lights are harder to see than car brake lights. Flashing your brake light helps other drivers notice it. Flash your brake light before slowing down in unexpected places, like the middle of a block or near an alley.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your chance of a crash?

options.text: Use your turn signals to show you plan to change lanes.
Follow other drivers closely.
Keep your eyes focused only 15 feet ahead of your motorcycle.
Do not use your headlight during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals to show you plan to change lanes.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make yourself visible, tell others your plans, keep safe distance, look ahead at least 12 seconds, spot hazards, and be ready to react to changes.

questions.question: What kind of penalties apply to drinking and riding?

options.text: Severe.
Up to a judge to decide.
Not very harsh.
Optional.

questions.explanation: Oregon law has severe mandatory penalties for drinking and riding. It is illegal and dangerous to ride while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: When being passed, which of the following is NOT a hazard?

options.text: Extended mirrors.
Objects being thrown from other vehicles.
Wind blasts.
Headlights.

questions.explanation: When being passed, watch out for the passing vehicle's mirrors, wind gusts, and objects thrown by passengers. These are real dangers to avoid.

questions.question: What should you do if you are riding next to another vehicle?

options.text: Speed up or slow down.
Wave at the other driver.
Stay alongside until the next exit.
Let the other driver worry about it.

questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous because you may be in its blind spot. The vehicle could also block your way to escape if a hazard appears. Speed up or drop back to get out of this position.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly?

options.text: Use the front brake only.
Use the rear brake first.
Release the throttle and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time. Brake firmly and do not panic if the brakes lock.

questions.question: When making a normal stop, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Use only the rear brake to save the front brake.
Use only the front brake to save the rear brake.
Squeeze the front brake sharply.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Build a habit of using both brakes every time you slow or stop. If you develop this habit, it will be easier to use both brakes correctly in a quick stop.

questions.question: What should you do when it starts raining?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull off to the side of the road until the rain stops.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Increase your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: In wet conditions, avoid riding in the center of the lane. Instead, ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you. The left tire track is often best, but it depends on traffic and road conditions.

questions.question: The body removes about one alcoholic drink per hour. If a person drinks seven drinks in three hours, how many drinks will likely remain in their system three hours after their last drink?

options.text: Two
Three
Four
Five

questions.explanation: To find drinks remaining, subtract the number of hours passed from the total drinks consumed. A person who drinks seven drinks in three hours will have about four drinks left in their system three hours later.

questions.question: Riding next to another rider:

options.text: Lets you use more of the road.
Should be avoided because it limits your escape routes.
Lets you talk to each other.
Makes it easier for cars to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be avoided because it limits your escape routes.
questions.explanation: Do not ride next to another motorcycle. This limits both riders' ability to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: When riding in a group, the best way to stay close while keeping safe distance is to ride:

options.text: In pairs.
In a staggered formation.
In a single-file line.
In a passing formation.

questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps riders close while giving each person enough space to stay safe. Use single-file when riding around curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway. Never ride side-by-side.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle properly, you should:

options.text: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up.
Sit far back on the seat so you can keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Drag your feet on the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up.
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms control the motorcycle rather than hold you up. Your arms should be slightly bent at the grips. Keep your knees against the gas tank and your feet firmly on the footrests to help with balance.

questions.question: Which formation keeps group riders closest together?

options.text: Pyramid
Staggered
Single-file
Compressed

questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps riders close while letting each person maintain safe distance. Use single-file when taking curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: A motorcyclist is well-protected when wearing:

options.text: A jacket with exposed arms.
Boots with tall heels.
Leather gloves.
Shoes that stop below the ankle.

questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that fully cover your arms and legs. Boots or shoes should be tall and sturdy to cover and support your ankles. Footwear should have low heels that won't catch on foot pegs or road surfaces. Leather or durable gloves protect your hands in a crash and improve your grip on the controls.

questions.question: Reflective material on your helmet:

options.text: Helps other drivers see you.
Is not allowed.
Should only be used at night.
Does not help you be seen.

questions.explanation: Reflective material on a vest or helmet makes you more visible to other drivers. Use it both day and night.

questions.question: When braking, you should use:

options.text: The front brake only.
The rear brake only.
Both front and rear brakes.
Either the front or rear brake, but not both.

questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: A face shield:

options.text: Protects your eyes and face.
Is not recommended.
Is required.
Does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, impact-resistant face shield gives the best protection for your eyes and face. Glasses or sunglasses are not enough. In Vermont, eye or face protection is not legally required if your motorcycle has a windshield, but it is recommended.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Be flexible about your lane position and adjust to changing conditions.
Travel faster than usual to reach your destination quickly.
Always use your low beam to see better.
Stay very close to the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be flexible about your lane position and adjust to changing conditions.
questions.explanation: Be flexible about your lane position when riding at night. Use safe riding strategies in difficult conditions.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should travel:

options.text: Slower than you would during the day under the same conditions.
At the same speed as you would during the day under the same conditions.
Faster than you would during the day under the same conditions.
On the shoulder of the road so other vehicles can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slower than you would during the day under the same conditions.
questions.explanation: Ride slower at night than you would during the day in similar weather and traffic. It is harder to see hazards in the dark. Slowing down helps you avoid accidents.

questions.question: The best lane position:

options.text: Is always on the right side of the lane.
Is always in the center of the lane.
Is always on the left side of the lane.
Changes based on the road, weather, and traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Changes based on the road, weather, and traffic.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Change your position based on road, weather, and traffic conditions.

questions.question: If your motorcycle begins to wobble, you should:

options.text: Keep riding, as the wobble will fix itself.
Brake quickly.
Slow down by closing the throttle.
Speed up quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down by closing the throttle.
questions.explanation: Speeding up will make the wobble worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slow down gradually by closing the throttle. Lean forward and down, then pull off the road. Find and fix the cause of the wobble.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not needed if you have a windshield.
Only protects your eyes.
Protects your face and eyes.
Does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face and eyes. Goggles protect only your eyes, not your face. A windshield is not a good substitute for either.

questions.question: Engine braking:

options.text: Is illegal.
Is slowing down by turning off the engine.
Is slowing down by downshifting.
Is not encouraged because it damages the engine.

questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear slows your motorcycle, similar to applying the brakes. This is called engine braking.
